toyota_summary:
China's economy grew just 4.3 percent in the first half of 2026, a record low, yet Beijing is refusing to expand stimulus spending. The government's reluctance to inject cash into demand suggests automakers will face continued weakness in the world's largest vehicle market, with consumers postponing purchases and price competition intensifying. Watch whether Beijing shifts course by the end of the third quarter.

Europe's auto regulatory package is stuck in early-stage negotiations with the parliament, buried under hundreds of proposed amendments that won't be resolved until year-end at the earliest. The delay means manufacturers can't yet finalize compliance strategies for emissions, battery standards, or tariffs, forcing investment decisions into limbo. Any major revisions to EV mandates or tariff provisions could upend production planning across the continent.

Hungary's former foreign minister has joined Chinese EV maker BYD in a senior role, signaling Beijing's push to embed political relationships into its European expansion. This move suggests Chinese automakers will use government connections and local influence to navigate regulatory obstacles and secure favorable conditions in ways Western competitors cannot easily replicate.

emails.summary_en: Former Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó has resigned from parliament to take a senior executive role at BYD, overseeing external relations and new business development for the Chinese EV maker. The move drew criticism from Prime Minister Péter Magyar, who accused Szijjártó of previously lobbying for state subsidies to BYD while in government. The appointment comes as BYD prepares to begin production at its major new Hungarian plant later this year.
emails.summary_ja: ハンガリーのシーヤールトー前外相が議員を辞職し、中国のEV大手BYDで対外関係・新事業開発を担当する幹部職に就くことを発表した。マジャル首相はこれを批判し、同氏が政府在任中にBYDへの国家補助金を働きかけていたと非難した。BYDは今年中にハンガリーの新工場で生産を開始する予定で、同国を欧州における主要生産拠点としている。
